<!-- Please refer to our contributing documentation for any questions on submitting a pull request, or let us know here if you need any help: https://ionicframework.com/docs/building/contributing -->

## Pull request checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been reviewed and added / updated if needed (for bug fixes / features)
  - Some docs updates need to be made in the `ionic-docs` repo, in a separate PR. See the [contributing guide](https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-framework/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#modifying-documentation) for details.
- [x] Build (`npm run build`) was run locally and any changes were pushed
- [x] Lint (`npm run lint`) has passed locally and any fixes were made for failures


## Pull request type

<!-- Please do not submit updates to dependencies unless it fixes an issue. --> 

<!-- Please try to limit your pull request to one type, submit multiple pull requests if needed. --> 

Please check the type of change your PR introduces:
- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, renaming)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other (please describe): 


## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying. -->
While documenting item and adding a playground for customizing the input highlight, I noticed that `--highlight-height` being set was no longer showing the highlight in `ios` mode. Here is the documentation that explains how this should work: https://ionicframework.com/docs/api/item#input-highlight

It looks like the code for this to work was removed by this commit: https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-framework/commit/5ca2ce91971408218d7bdc52509ce61a6ebb46aa#diff-c74ddc9584918db0c15a8ba1db280abfe14e7f7632b84e1dfbf74ce86315c6c3L378

<!-- Issues are required for both bug fixes and features. -->
Issue URL: I could not find any open issues for this 


## What is the new behavior?
<!-- Please describe the behavior or changes that are being added by this PR. -->

- Adds the removed code back to `item.scss` to make it work with iOS again
- Adds a test in `item/test/highlight` that applies focus to all of the items while showing the different states
- Updates the `item/test/fill` test to add a row of items with focus to see the behavior better
- Adds playwright for both of the above tests

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this introduces a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->


## Other information

<!-- Any other information that is important to this PR such as screenshots of how the component looks before and after the change. -->

### Item: Fill Before & After

In this test you can see that the iOS highlight does not show until `--highlight-height` is set for the last item.

| | Before | After |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `ios`| ![localhost_3333_src_components_item_test_fill_ionic_mode=ios (1)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6577830/189376738-0eee3954-0c8f-4e44-bf32-8270e1d5b651.png) | ![localhost_3333_src_components_item_test_fill_ionic_mode=ios](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6577830/189378420-8ca6f9fd-3686-4f3c-a4df-cdd5300f4367.png) |

### Item: Highlight Before & After

For this test I have set the `--highlight-height` for all custom items, so all iOS items in the last 2 sections should show a highlight.

| | Before | After |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `ios`| ![localhost_3333_src_components_item_test_highlight_ionic_mode=ios](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6577830/189377156-f19885fb-76a2-474c-8db8-0f652cb595fa.png) | ![localhost_3333_src_components_item_test_highlight_ionic_mode=ios](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6577830/189378683-ea0a729a-3a47-4f56-8393-62fe4582f3e5.png) |

I did not change this test at all, it should be the same before & after my change.

| `md` | ![localhost_3333_src_components_item_test_form](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6577830/189377666-1ac910bc-9d57-4977-935b-34558f630543.png) | ![localhost_3333_src_components_item_test_form](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6577830/189378794-95ad2d9c-c07c-417c-add0-8cd012ad0999.png) |

comments.body:
Question for this configuration used in both tests - were you observing horizontal clipping of the screenshot viewport? 

Based on the screenshot captures, I think this can likely be removed if not.

```ts
await page.setIonViewport();
```

The `resizeViewportWidth` option was introduced for 1 item test we have, where the rendered contents are larger than the device width (some legacy test that renders on like a landscape tablet viewport width).
Oh no I just copied from another test, but also I saw that `setIonViewport` was used to take a full height screenshot so I thought that would make it work. I don't think it did though ha.
The `resizeViewportWidth` option can also likely be removed from the `fill` test. `setIonViewport` by itself will handle resizing the height 👍
